questions.question: Which of the following does NOT show bad brakes?

options.text: Pads that are clean and dry

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads that are clean and dry
questions.explanation: When you inspect brakes, look for cracked drums, shoes or pads covered in oil or grease, and shoes that are worn too thin. Clean, dry pads are a sign of good brakes.

questions.question: How can you avoid distracted driving?

options.text: Set your radio stations before you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Set your radio stations before you drive.
questions.explanation: To avoid distracted driving, set your radio and mirrors before you start driving. Plan your route ahead of time. Do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving. Avoid difficult conversations with passengers.

questions.question: If the letter "G" appears in Column 1 of a hazardous materials shipping paper, what else must be included?

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous material

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous material
questions.explanation: The letter "G" means a generic name is being used. A generic name must always include the technical name of the material.

questions.question: Who is responsible for safe vehicle operation?
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for safe vehicle operation. Always inspect your vehicle before driving a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees be trained?

options.text: At least once every three years

questions.correctAnswerText: At least once every three years
questions.explanation: Employees who work with hazardous materials must receive training and testing at least once every three years.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes several times before pressing hard on the pedal.
Press the brake pedal as hard as possible every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way in vehicles with or without ABS. ABS automatically prevents the wheels from locking when you apply the brakes.

questions.question: What happens if one-fourth of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing?

options.text: The driver can drive at reduced speeds.
The vehicle must be taken out of service until it is repaired.
The vehicle is safe to drive since most of the spring remains.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle must be taken out of service until it is repaired.
questions.explanation: If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing from a leaf spring, the vehicle is unsafe. It must be taken out of service and repaired.

questions.question: What does keeping cargo low do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Helps prevent rollover
questions.explanation: Keeping cargo close to the ground lowers the vehicle's center of gravity. This helps prevent rollovers when turning.

questions.question: Which is an example of required emergency equipment?
questions.correctAnswerText: A spare electrical fuse
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have spare electrical fuses, reflective triangles or flares, and a working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: Keeps air in the brake system if there is a serious leak
Prevents the truck from being stolen
Prevents the driver from driving too fast

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in the brake system if there is a serious leak
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve closes automatically if air pressure drops too low. This keeps air in the brake system if a trailer breaks away or develops a leak.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel toward the direction you want to go.
Turn the steering wheel away from the direction you want to go.
Turn the wheel as far as it will go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel away from the direction you want to go.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, first turn the steering wheel away from the direction you want to go. Once the trailer starts to turn, turn the wheel the other way to follow the trailer.

questions.question: What is a problem with retarders?

options.text: They help slow down a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are not legal everywhere.
questions.explanation: A retarder is a device that helps slow a vehicle and reduces brake use. However, retarders can be loud and are not allowed in all areas.

questions.question: Why should cargo tanks never be completely full?

options.text: The liquid needs room to expand when it gets warm.
Rules require three feet of space between the liquid and the top of the tank.
A full tank would be too heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: The liquid needs room to expand when it gets warm.
questions.explanation: Liquids expand as they get warmer. Drivers must leave extra space in a tank for this expansion. Different liquids expand different amounts, so drivers must know the expansion requirements for their specific load.

questions.question: If brakes fail while going down a long hill, what should the driver do?

options.text: Turn the vehicle off and then back on to fix the brakes.
Look for an escape ramp or another way to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for an escape ramp or another way to stop.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail going downhill, the best option is to use an escape ramp. If no escape ramp is available, look for another escape route, such as a side road or open field.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that you slow down other drivers, what should you do?

options.text: Wave your arm out the window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and hold up traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you (if local laws allow it).

questions.question: ____ are used to warn others about hazardous materials.
questions.correctAnswerText: Placards
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs called placards are placed on cargo packages and vehicle sides to warn drivers about hazardous materials. The shipper puts on the placards, and the driver must make sure they are correct.

questions.question: When inspecting your tires before a trip, what should you check?
questions.correctAnswerText: The tire pressure.
questions.explanation: When inspecting your tires before a trip, check that the tire pressure is correct—not too low and not too high.

questions.question: Front-to-back liquid surge is usually strongest in:
questions.correctAnswerText: Tanks without baffles.
questions.explanation: Smooth bore tanks, also called unbaffled tanks, have nothing to slow liquid movement. This makes them likely to have strong front-to-back liquid surge.

questions.question: If a vehicle comes with an inspection report from the previous driver, what should you do?

options.text: Inspect the vehicle first, then compare your notes to the report.
Review the report first when you start your inspection.
Skip your own inspection and just use the report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Review the report first when you start your inspection.
questions.explanation: The first step of a vehicle inspection is to review any report left by the previous driver.

questions.question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Make hand gestures at other drivers.
Assume other drivers have good reasons for what they do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers have good reasons for what they do.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, give other drivers the benefit of the doubt. Assume they have valid reasons for their actions and don't take what they do personally.
